episodes.title: The Lion Capital's Long Journey
sources: Wikipedia, 'Lion Capital of Ashoka' and 'State Emblem of India' (read 2026-11-17), citing ASI excavation reports (F. O. Oertel, 1904-05) and Constituent Assembly proceedings of July and December 1947

quiz.q: When was the Sarnath Lion Capital excavated?
quiz.why: F. O. Oertel of the ASI excavated it in the 1904–05 winter season.

quiz.q: What was adapted from the capital for the national flag?
quiz.why: The wheel on the abacus was the model for the flag's wheel.

quiz.q: From which text is the motto 'Satyameva Jayate' taken?
quiz.why: The motto is a quote from the Mundaka Upanishad.

review.note: Facts were read against the pages listed. Sources are secondary (Wikipedia); original ASI and Constituent Assembly records were not reachable. Sources disagree on the date (c. 250 BCE or 280 BCE), so the video says 'about the third century BCE'. The object speaks in the first person, a storytelling device. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: Konark: a Temple Built as a Chariot
sources: NCERT, An Introduction to Indian Art Part I (Class XI Fine Art, 2020-21), ch. 6 'Temple Architecture and Sculpture': Odisha section, Konark, pp. 78-80 (archive.org ncert-kefa1, read 2026-11-17)

quiz.q: What are the great wheels at Konark said to represent?
options: Chariot wheels of the Sun god
The wheel of law on a flag
quiz.why: NCERT: twelve pairs of wheels represent the chariot wheels of the Sun god.

quiz.q: What is the hall before an Odisha deul called?
quiz.why: Deuls are preceded by mandapas called jagamohana in Odisha.

quiz.q: Why did Konark's great tower fall?
options: It proved too heavy for its site
It was pulled down for stone
quiz.why: NCERT: the shikhara, said to reach 70 m, proved too heavy for its site and fell in the nineteenth century.

review.note: Facts were read against the source listed. NCERT says the tower is 'said to have reached' 70 m and the pavilion is 'said to be' the largest enclosed space in Hindu architecture. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: The Cloud Messenger's Route
sources: H. H. Wilson, The Megha Duta, or Cloud Messenger (1813), public domain, archive.org mghadta00kali

quiz.q: Where does the cloud rest on the Mango Peak, thought to be the source of the Narmada?
quiz.why: Wilson identifies Amracuta with the mountain commonly called Amarkantak.

quiz.q: Which river does Wilson identify as the modern Vetravati?
quiz.why: Wilson's note: the Vetravati is the modern Betwa, passing Bhilsa (Vidisha).

quiz.q: What kind of poem is the Meghaduta?
quiz.why: Its device of a message carried by a cloud spawned the sandesa kavya genre.

review.note: Facts were read against the sources listed. Modern place identifications follow Wilson and are hedged in the script; the map is schematic and Alaka is mythical. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: Ajanta: Caves Lost and Found
sources: Wikipedia, 'Ajanta Caves' (read 2026-11-17), citing ASI, UNESCO entry 242 and W. M. Spink

quiz.q: In what year were the Ajanta caves brought to wider attention by John Smith?
quiz.why: On 28 April 1819, while hunting tigers, he was shown Cave 10 by a local boy.

quiz.q: Which river flows through the gorge at Ajanta?
quiz.why: The caves are in the U-shaped gorge of the River Waghur.

quiz.q: Which dynasty ruled during the main second phase of work at Ajanta?
quiz.why: The later caves belong to the Vakataka period, mainly the reign of Harisena.

review.note: Facts were read against the source listed. The 460-480 CE dating is Spink's argument; older accounts give 400-650 CE. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: Xuanzang Comes to Nalanda
sources: Samuel Beal, The Life of Hiuen-Tsiang by the Shaman Hwui Li (public domain), archive.org b28983841, Book III and Introduction

quiz.q: Who was the head of Nalanda when Xuanzang arrived?
quiz.why: Huili's account names Silabhadra as the revered head, called Treasure of the Good Law.

quiz.q: About how many monks, residents and visitors, were at Nalanda in the account?
quiz.why: The priests, residents or strangers, always reach 10,000.

quiz.q: How did Nalanda meet its costs, according to the account?
quiz.why: The king remitted the revenues of about 100 villages for its endowment.

review.note: Facts were read against the source listed (Beal's translation of Huili's account). Numbers are as stated by the source and may be round. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: Xuanzang's Road
sources: Wikipedia, 'Xuanzang' (read 2026-11-18), summarising Xuanzang's Records and Huili's Life
Samuel Beal, The Life of Hiuen-Tsiang (public domain), archive.org b28983841

quiz.q: In which year did Xuanzang return to Chang'an?
quiz.why: He arrived on the seventh day of the first month of 645, sixteen years after leaving.

quiz.q: Which famous centre of learning in Bihar did he study at?
quiz.why: He studied at Nalanda under Silabhadra.

quiz.q: What is the title of his travelogue?
quiz.why: The Records of the Western Regions (Xiyu ji) is a key source on seventh-century India.

review.note: Facts were read against the sources listed. The departure year is disputed (627 or 629) and the script says so; the map is schematic. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: Hampi's Market, Seen by a Traveller
sources: Robert Sewell, A Forgotten Empire (Vijayanagar) (1900), public domain: Narrative of Domingos Paes (written probably 1520-22), archive.org aforgottenempir00paesgoog, read 2026-11-17

quiz.q: Which Portuguese traveller described Vijayanagara around 1520?
quiz.why: His chronicle was written probably in 1520-22 and printed in Sewell's A Forgotten Empire.

quiz.q: What did Paes say the city seemed as large as?
quiz.why: What he could see of it seemed as large as Rome.

quiz.q: Why is a traveller's account a source to read with care?
quiz.why: Such accounts are valuable but reflect what one outsider saw and understood.

review.note: Facts were read against the source listed. Every claim is Paes's own report, framed as a traveller's account. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: Ibn Battuta at the Sultan's Court
sources: NCERT, Themes in Indian History Part II (Class XII), ch. 5, archive.org ncert-lehs2, read 2026-11-17

quiz.q: What office did the Sultan give Ibn Battuta in Delhi?
quiz.why: NCERT: the Sultan was impressed by his scholarship and appointed him qazi of Delhi.

quiz.q: What was the foot-post of the Delhi Sultanate called?
quiz.why: The foot-post was the dawa; the horse-post was the uluq.

quiz.q: Which book records Ibn Battuta's travels?
quiz.why: His book of travels, written in Arabic, is called the Rihla.

review.note: Facts were read against the sources listed. Rihla descriptions are Ibn Battuta's own account and may reflect his perspective. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: Kabir in Six Couplets
sources: NCERT, Themes in Indian History Part II (Class XII), ch. 6 'Bhakti-Sufi Traditions', section 8.1 and Source 10 (archive.org ncert-lehs2, read 2026-11-17)
Rabindranath Tagore, Songs of Kabir (1915), public domain (archive.org cu31924023165248), ideas paraphrased

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three main collections of verses attributed to Kabir?
quiz.why: The Tevaram is a Nayanar collection; Kabir's verses are in the Bijak, the Granthavali and the Adi Granth.

quiz.q: What is nirguna bhakti?
options: Worship of an abstract form of god
Worship of a god in human form
quiz.why: NCERT: nirguna bhakti was worship of an abstract form of god.

quiz.q: What is the special poetic language associated with Kabir and other nirguna poets called?
quiz.why: NCERT: some poems are composed in the special language of nirguna poets, the sant bhasha.

review.note: Facts were read against the sources listed. Verses attributed to Kabir survive in several traditions and NCERT notes that scholars cannot establish with certainty which are his; ideas here are paraphrased from the 1915 translation and NCERT. Retold lines: all six idea cards paraphrase attributed verses. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: Bhakti and Sufi Voices Across Centuries
sources: NCERT, Themes in Indian History Part II (Class XII), ch. 6 'Bhakti-Sufi Traditions' (archive.org ncert-lehs2, read 2026-11-17)

quiz.q: What is the Nalayira Divyaprabandham sometimes called?
quiz.why: This Alvar anthology was frequently described as the Tamil Veda.

quiz.q: In which language are the vachanas of the Virashaivas composed?
quiz.why: NCERT: our understanding of the Virashaiva tradition comes from vachanas composed in Kannada.

quiz.q: Which Sikh Guru compiled the Adi Granth Sahib?
quiz.why: NCERT: the fifth preceptor, Guru Arjan, compiled Guru Nanak's hymns with others' in the Adi Granth Sahib.

review.note: Facts were read against the source listed. NCERT gives approximate periods for these teachers and notes that Kabir's verses survive in later compilations. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none.
